raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Two DeepSeek-V4.1 decode kernels lose time to grid shape on GPUs whose SMs hold 1024 resident threads (CC 10.7 / sm_107), not to memory bandwidth:

- `amax8_varlen` (two-level indexer block keys) sizes `grid.y` from the logits buffer width (`max_compressed_seq_len`), but rows only hold `compressed_seq_lens` keys. At 128K context about 85% of the 512-thread CTAs exit after reading `seq_len`; at 2 CTAs/SM that is dozens of waves of empty CTAs.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` launches 640-thread CTAs for hidden 5120. Two do not fit a 1024-thread SM, so the quant CTAs plus the pad CTAs run in two waves.

## Modifications

- `block_amax.cuh`: cap `grid.y` at two waves of resident CTAs (occupancy API, cached per device) and grid-stride over key chunks.
- `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`: when two one-chunk-per-thread CTAs do not fit an SM (`cudaDevAttrMaxThreadsPerMultiProcessor`), launch half the threads with two 16B chunks each (both loads issued before the quant-group reductions) and two pad slots per thread. On 2048-thread SMs the launch is unchanged.
- Both per-device host queries are cached with `init_once`. The two-chunk launch is used only when `top_k <= num_chunks / 2`, so no previously valid `top_k` is rejected.

Both kernels produce bitwise-identical outputs (all outputs compared, including pad slots and the scale swizzle).

## Accuracy Tests

On sm_107 (CC 10.7), at this PR's head (merged with main, including #46090):

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py`: 6 passed. The new `test_hidden_5120_two_chunk_matches_one_chunk` quantizes the same rows with `top_k=6` (two chunks per thread on 1024-thread SMs) and `top_k=384` (one-chunk fallback) and requires identical FP8 bytes and scales, plus correct top-k copies and padding.
- Both kernels are bitwise identical to main's versions at the decode shapes below (all outputs, including pad slots).

Not yet run: an end-to-end GSM8K run. CI hardware (2048-thread SMs) takes only the one-chunk path.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

sm_107 (CC 10.7), this PR vs main's kernels, one GPU, 43 calls captured in one CUDA graph (amax: 4-6), hot = one buffer set, cold = rotated buffers, ABBA-interleaved replays, median time per call, this PR vs main:

| kernel | case | hot | cold |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| amax8_varlen | rows 198, ctx 32K | -80.6% | -75.4% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 198, ctx 128K | -68.5% | -56.8% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 342, ctx 32K | -84.6% | -78.9% |
| amax8_varlen | rows 342, ctx 128K | -63.2% | -60.3% |
| mega_moe_pre_dispatch | rows 198 | -15.3% | +1.4% |
| mega_moe_pre_dispatch | rows 342 | -27.4% | -26.9% |

These two kernels are a small share of a decode step, so no end-to-end number is claimed. #46090 edits other lines of `mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests (hidden 5120 path comparison in `test_mega_moe_pre_dispatch.py`; the two-chunk path only triggers on 1024-thread SMs).
- [ ] Update documentation as needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (kernel level).

files.patch:
@@ -121,5 +121,43 @@ def test_topk_weight_scale_matches_torch_multiply(scale: float) -> None:
     assert torch.all(buf_weights[num_tokens:] == 0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10,
+    reason="Requires Blackwell GPU (sm_100+)",
+)
+def test_hidden_5120_two_chunk_matches_one_chunk() -> None:
+    """top_k=6 takes the two-chunk path on 1024-thread SMs, top_k=384 the one-chunk path."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_tokens, padded_max, hidden = 198, 512, 5120
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 3
+
+    def dispatch(top_k: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        topk_idx = torch.randint(
+            0, 384, (num_tokens, top_k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        topk_weights = torch.rand(num_tokens, top_k, device="cuda")
+        buf_x = torch.empty(
+            padded_max, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        )
+        buf_x_sf = torch.empty(
+            padded_max, hidden // 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        buf_idx = torch.empty(padded_max, top_k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+        buf_weights = torch.empty(padded_max, top_k, device="cuda")
+        mega_moe_pre_dispatch(
+            x, topk_idx, topk_weights, buf_x, buf_x_sf, buf_idx, buf_weights
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(buf_idx[:num_tokens], topk_idx.to(torch.int64))
+        assert torch.equal(buf_weights[:num_tokens], topk_weights)
+        assert torch.all(buf_idx[num_tokens:] == -1)
+        assert torch.all(buf_weights[num_tokens:] == 0)
+        return buf_x[:num_tokens].view(torch.uint8), buf_x_sf[:num_tokens]
+
+    q_two_chunk, sf_two_chunk = dispatch(6)
+    q_one_chunk, sf_one_chunk = dispatch(384)
+    assert torch.equal(q_two_chunk, q_one_chunk)
+    assert torch.equal(sf_two_chunk, sf_one_chunk)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))
